blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Enforcement of Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights
A Fundamental Right (Supreme Court cannot refuse)
A Discretionary Remedy (High Court may refuse)
Applicable across the entire territory of India
Restricted to the respective State or Union Territory jurisdiction

items: Fundamental Rights under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 352.
High Courts under Article 226 have a wider writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court under Article 32 as they can enforce legal rights in addition to Fundamental Rights.
President's Rule under Article 356 requires parliamentary approval within two months from the date of issue.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 14 guarantees Equality before Law and Equal Protection of Laws within India.
Article 21 ensures Protection of Life and Personal Liberty, forming the bedrock of modern Indian legal jurisprudence.
Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly.
Article 280 provides for the establishment of a Finance Commission every five years by the President.
Article 368 details the procedure and power of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
